title: openGym: the free, self-hosted workout tracker
notes: Facts checked 2026-10-10: github.com/DuarteSantos8/openGym (README: self-hosted, AGPL-3.0, docker compose up, no subscription/ads/telemetry, data in ./data, over 5,600 exercises with animated demos browsable by muscle on a body map, guided sessions with pre-filled weights, rest timer and PR detection, plate math, progression rules incl. deloads on stalls, muscle map in three modes, imports from FitNotes/Strong/Hevy, passkeys, offline, sync, optional AI coach you approve, HTTPS on a domain for phone passkeys, iPhone as a PWA, standalone Android app with no server; created 2026-07-18; 8,797 stars, +6,749 in the trending week on 2026-10-10). The narration is Chatterbox (MIT) on the laptop's CPU. Also: filter exercises by the equipment you own; two devices editing at once merge field by field; a read-only, local MCP server so an assistant like Claude Desktop can answer questions about your training history.

lines.text: Most gym apps keep your workouts on their servers, and push you toward a subscription.
say: Most gym apps keep your workouts on their servers, and push you toward a subscription.

lines.text: openGym runs on yours. And this week, it picked up nearly 7,000 GitHub stars.

lines.text: One Docker command, and it's live on your own machine. No ads, no subscription, no telemetry.

lines.text: Your whole training history sits in one folder. Back it up, and you've backed up everything.
